text:
mia: Heads up — nightly CI fired a perf alert on the runtime harness for kernel-selector v3.2. p99 token latency jumped ~18% for redwood-v1-7b compared to baseline.

ci-bot: Alert: nightly-bench/1910002345: p99 latency delta +18% (threshold 10%) for model redwood-v1-7b, kernel v3.2. Links: https://ci.redwood/influx/alerts/1910002345 :warning:

sam: ugh. first pass — is KV cache warmup accounted for in this run? those synthetic replays sometimes miss prefix warmup and look worse.

mia: good call. alert payload shows sample_size=64, no explicit warmup. harness uses synthetic traffic with randomized seeds.

jorge: can we rerun a deterministic replay with warmup and kernel pinned? propose: `ci replay --seed 1234 --model redwood-v1-7b --kernel v3.2 --warmup 300 --samples 200`

asha: also add KV hit ratio and kernel selection histogram to the run. last time a subtle change in selector heuristics bumped fallback to slower kernel for long sequences.

linh: attaching a tiny log excerpt from the failing job that the alert referenced:
```
[2026-03-12T03:15:12Z] kernel-selector: chosen=fast_attn_v2 (fallback_count=3)
[2026-03-12T03:15:12Z] kv-cache: hits=12 misses=48 hit_rate=20% (cold start)
[2026-03-12T03:15:13Z] latency: p50=34ms p90=78ms p99=212ms
```

sam: hit_rate 20% screams warmup. synthetic workload probably had short prefixes. That will amplify kernel overhead for kv-miss paths.

mia: action items: 1) rerun deterministic replay with warmup=300 and samples=200 (jorge will queue), 2) temporary change to alerting: smooth p99 with moving-median over 3 runs to reduce noise, 3) add KV hit-rate & selected-kernel metrics to the alert payload.

jorge: queued rerun -> job 1910003001. I'll include 3 different seeds (1234, 2345, 3456) and attach per-seed histograms.

ci-bot: Job queued: nightly-rerun/1910003001 by jorge. Config: model=redwood-v1-7b kernel=v3.2 warmup=300 samples=200 seeds=[1234,2345,3456].

asha: for flaky triage — recommend we mark this as flaky if the reruns have >10% variance between seeds. Otherwise treat as regression and bisect kernel-selector changes between v3.1->v3.2.

mia: agreed. if reruns confirm regression we'll run a canary that compares v3.1 vs v3.2 apples-to-apples with identical replay trace and kv-state snapshot.

linh: note: we should also log kernel-selection decision context (sequence_len, quantized_profile id) so we can reproduce selector path. adding that to the harness now.

sam: small stabilization tweak suggestion for alerts: use p90 + 1.5 * IQR instead of raw p99 threshold; quieter and less sensitive to outliers from rare cold starts.

mia: good idea. I'll put a PR up to change alerting rule to use the IQR-based guard and add a brief note in the alert message about sample size and kv-warmup.

jorge: update: rerun finished for seed 1234. preliminary numbers: p99 delta vs baseline = +3% (warmup=300), kv hit_rate ~72%. looks like warmup explains most of the spike. still running other seeds.

mia: great — hold off on bisect until all seeds finish. we'll close the alert if all seeds are within 5% of baseline.

asha: I'll draft a short runbook section on 'CI perf alert triage' recommending deterministic replay, required metadata (kv-hit, kernel-hist), and when to mark flaky.

sam: thanks — that should cut down on noisy wakeups. :coffee:

mia: ok closing loop: PR for alert smoothing + add metrics -> me. runbook draft -> asha. canary/bisect plan -> TBD if reruns still fail.

ci-bot: Alert closed automatically (policy: noise_mitigation).
